title: On the Computational Complexity of Guided Berry Phase Estimation
abstract: We prove that deciding the Berry phase for parameterised 2-local qubit Hamiltonians is BQP-complete when presented with a classical description of a guiding state, promised to overlap with the ground state of the system. Our results extend to systems with weighted Heisenberg interactions and when restricted to a 2D square or triangular lattice geometry. The techniques we develop leverage the Schrieffer--Wolff transformation, typically used in the construction of perturbative gadget reductions for local Hamiltonian problems, extending it to parameterised families of Hamiltonians. We demonstrate that there exists a choice of parameterised simulator Hamiltonians whose Berry phase well-approximates that of a parameterised target family. Using the perturbative gadget reduction framework of Oliveira and Terhal and of Schuch and Verstraete, we adapt the arguments to parameterised interactions and demonstrate the error bounds in the resulting simulation can be controlled. Additionally, we provide an explicit proof that families of 1-local Hamiltonians have a Berry phase that can be efficiently computed to inverse-polynomial precision. This establishes a complexity transition between 1-local and 2-local Hamiltonian families.
summary: This work establishes the computational complexity of estimating the Berry phase for parameterized quantum systems, proving it is BQP-complete for 2-local interactions. By developing advanced simulation techniques, the authors also show a critical complexity transition, proving that 1-local Hamiltonians allow for efficient, polynomial-time computation of the Berry phase.
main_problem: The paper determines the computational complexity of deciding the Berry phase for parameterized local qubit Hamiltonians.
main_result: It proves that this problem is BQP-complete for 2-local Hamiltonians, while establishing that the problem for 1-local Hamiltonians can be solved in polynomial time (P).
method: The techniques involve extending the Schrieffer-Wolff transformation to parameterized families and utilizing the perturbative gadget reduction framework to control simulation errors.
model_or_system: The study focuses on parameterised 2-local qubit Hamiltonians, specifically on square or triangular lattices, and extends to weighted Heisenberg interactions.
key_observables: The Berry phase ($\vartheta$), which is the primary observable whose computational complexity is analyzed.
important_parameters: The locality of interactions (1-local vs. 2-local), the required precision ($\epsilon_{	ext{alg}}$), and the initial overlap ($\delta_0$) of the guiding state.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on constructing simulator Hamiltonians that accurately approximate the target Hamiltonian up to second order, and the hardness proof requires the existence of a guiding state with sufficient overlap.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the locality of the Hamiltonian relative to known complexity results, and schematics detail the logical flow connecting uniform simulation, Schrieffer-Wolff analysis, and gadget reductions.
paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing uniform simulation techniques for parameterized Hamiltonians, extending these to the Schrieffer-Wolff analysis, applying gadget reductions to control errors, and culminating in the hardness proof (BQP-completeness) and the polynomial-time algorithm for 1-local cases.
why_interesting: It provides rigorous complexity results for physically relevant quantities (Berry phases) in quantum simulation, directly impacting the theoretical understanding of what quantum computers can efficiently calculate regarding geometric phases.
